chapter ends with open questions at its own level of detail. This first set
asks what the larger Architecture 2.0 effort must make possible.

**Building a usable design capability.** The moonshot requires both an
executable description of the current architecture problem and reusable
knowledge that can help without displacing authoritative project state.

- **How can compact system intent become an executable architecture
  specification without losing system obligations?** The specification must
  carry workload behavior, software semantics, interfaces, physical limits,
  and acceptance conditions into tools even when the original request leaves
  some of them implicit. Research can examine how to expose those missing
  obligations without replacing the architect's intent with assumptions made
  by the system.

- **What architecture knowledge can transfer across projects, and how can a
  design system detect when it no longer applies?** Prior designs can save
  repeated work, yet their assumptions may fail silently after workloads,
  software, tools, or implementation conditions change. The challenge is to
  make that loss of applicability visible before reused knowledge produces an
  unsupported architecture result.

**Establishing progress toward the moonshot.** Architecture 2.0 must improve
the resulting architecture, reduce the total cost of reaching a comparable
result, or do both.

- **Where does AI assistance create net value after its complete cost is
  counted?** A faster local step may not reduce the complete effort once data
  preparation, simulation, verification, failed work, and human review are
  included. The unresolved question is whether assistance improves the final
  architecture result, lowers the total cost of reaching it, or merely moves
  work elsewhere.

- **What minimum evidence should accompany a claimed Architecture 2.0
  advance?** Architecture results often depend on proprietary designs, tools,
  and physical data that cannot be disclosed, yet outside reviewers still need
  enough information to challenge the claim. A useful disclosure boundary must
  protect restricted material without making the claimed advance impossible to
  assess.

## Conclusion

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Mandate explicit specifications before commitment"}
A compact request is never a specification. Before treating any request as an
executable target, explicitly define the workload, software contract, system
boundary, legal alternatives, physical limits, acceptance checks, and intended
decision. While provisional assumptions allow early exploration, they strictly
cannot support architectural commitment. An isolated candidate may falsely
appear superior if the comparison omits a critical dependency or constraint.
Ensure every reported measurement traces to a verified evidence path before
committing to a design.
:::

The Lighthouse request gives the moonshot a fixed system-and-chip target
across workload, software, hardware, implementation, physical constraints,
verification, and the final recommendation. A coordinated design system may
use foundation or specialized models, prediction, generation, optimization,
retrieval, conventional algorithms, and tool-connected environments. None of
those components is the moonshot by itself. The capability lies in carrying
the architecture question through the complete work to a checked result,
technical recommendation, and separately owned commitment decision. It would
qualify as a useful new design method only if it makes that larger design object
expressible, executable, and checkable by people other than its creator.

The two tests keep the claims separate. The architecture comparison asks
whether a supported design meets the Lighthouse conditions. The comparison of
the complete approach asks whether assistance improves the result, lowers the
total cost of reaching a comparable result, or both. Current systems show
meaningful progress on individual tasks, but their evaluation cost, fidelity,
scope, and access to supporting material limit what they establish about the
complete challenge.

The moonshot matters only if present-day architecture work has become difficult
enough that additional assistance is worth investigating. The next chapter
examines the compounding sources of that difficulty
(@sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales).
